rationale: COMPANION SOURCE for perl/override-companion-resolve, pinned for its own sake rather than as an accessory. A cross-file override can only be resolved when the base's declaration set is KNOWN, so 'the base does not declare it' has to be checkable rather than assumed. override-companion-base declares `run`; override-companion-silent declares `unrelated` and deliberately NOT `gone`, which is what makes the withdrawn case decidable instead of indistinguishable from an absent base. Neither file needs an overrides edge of its own -- they are bases, not subclasses -- and this fixture asserts that.

forbidRelationships.note: a BASE declares a method, it does not override one. An overrides edge here would mean the companion pass invented a relationship no file states.
